strings.app.name: SalvaCiudad
strings.error.fatal.title: SalvaCiudad cannot start
strings.error.fatal.sdl: The system's graphics and input layer could not be started. Update your graphics drivers and try again.
strings.error.fatal.dataFolder: The folder for your settings and saved games could not be created. Check that you can write to your user folder.
strings.error.fatal.fonts: The game's fonts are missing or damaged. Reinstall the game.
strings.error.fatal.window: The game window could not be created.
strings.error.fatal.gpu: Your graphics card could not be used. SalvaCiudad needs a Direct3D 12 compatible graphics card with up-to-date drivers.
strings.notice.settings.quarantined: Your settings file was damaged and default settings are in use. The damaged file was kept as {0:file}.
strings.notice.settings.readOnly: Your settings were saved by a newer version of the game. They were loaded, but changes will not be saved so that version's settings are not lost.

notice.settings.ignored.one: {0} setting was not valid and went back to its default value.
notice.settings.ignored.other: {0} settings were not valid and went back to their default values.

strings.menu.main.singlePlayer.tooltip: Start a new game on your own.
strings.menu.main.hostGame.tooltip: Create a game for other players to join over the local network or by IP address.
strings.menu.main.joinGame.tooltip: Join a game hosted by another player.
strings.menu.main.mods.tooltip: Turn mods on or off and choose their load order.
strings.menu.main.settings.tooltip: Display, graphics, audio, controls, interface, language and game options.
strings.menu.background.saved: Menu background: seed {0} saved in your list.
strings.menu.background.notSaved: The seed {0} of the menu background could not be saved.
strings.dialog.comingSoon.title: Coming soon
strings.dialog.comingSoon.body: "{0:feature}" is not available yet. It will arrive in an upcoming version.
strings.dialog.displayFailed.title: Display change failed
strings.dialog.displayFailed.body: The system did not accept the new display setting. The previous one is still in use.
strings.dialog.keepDisplay.title: Keep these display settings?

dialog.keepDisplay.body.one: If you do not answer, the previous settings come back in {0} second.
dialog.keepDisplay.body.other: If you do not answer, the previous settings come back in {0} seconds.

strings.settings.title: Settings
strings.settings.restoreDefaults.tooltip: Put every option on this tab back to its default value.
strings.settings.display.mode.tooltip: Fullscreen gives the game the whole screen and may change its resolution. Borderless fills the screen without changing its resolution and makes switching to other programs faster. Windowed shows the game in a normal window.
strings.settings.display.monitor.tooltip: Screen used for fullscreen and borderless modes.
strings.settings.display.resolution.tooltip: Resolution used in fullscreen mode. "Desktop" keeps your monitor's current resolution.
strings.settings.display.vsync.tooltip: Matches the frame rate to your monitor to avoid tearing. Turn it off to lower input delay or to use a frame rate limit.
strings.settings.display.fpsLimit.tooltip: Maximum frames per second. A limit saves power and keeps the graphics card cooler.
strings.settings.display.fpsLimit.disabledToolti: Vertical sync already limits the frame rate. Turn it off to choose a limit.
strings.settings.graphics.preset.tooltip: Sets all the graphics options at once. Choosing an option below by hand switches to Custom.
strings.settings.graphics.shadows.tooltip: Quality of the shadows cast by the sun, buildings and villagers. Higher costs more performance.
strings.settings.graphics.drawDistance.tooltip: How far away detailed objects are still drawn.
strings.settings.graphics.vegetation.tooltip: Amount of grass, bushes and small plants.
strings.settings.graphics.antialiasing.tooltip: Smooths jagged edges. More samples look better and cost more performance.
strings.settings.audio.pendingNote: Sound effects and the ambient bed follow these volumes. Music comes later.
strings.settings.audio.master.tooltip: Volume of everything the game plays.
strings.settings.audio.effects.tooltip: Work, construction, combat and event sounds.
strings.settings.audio.ambient.tooltip: Wind, water, birds, weather and the sounds of the town.
strings.settings.controls.panSpeed.tooltip: How fast the camera moves with the keys or at the screen edge.
strings.settings.controls.zoomSpeed.tooltip: How much each turn of the mouse wheel zooms.
strings.settings.controls.invertZoom.tooltip: Swaps the direction of the mouse wheel for zooming.
strings.settings.controls.edgeScroll.tooltip: Moves the camera when the mouse pointer touches the edge of the screen.
strings.settings.controls.binding.tooltip: Click a key to change it for "{0:action}". Each action can have two keys.
strings.settings.controls.capture:
Press a key for "{0:action}".
Esc cancels. Delete removes the key.
strings.settings.controls.moved: {0:key} was used by "{1:action}"; that action no longer has it.
strings.settings.interface.scale.tooltip: Size of menus, text and windows, relative to your screen's scale setting.
strings.settings.interface.font.tooltip: Typeface used for menus and text.
strings.settings.interface.tooltips.tooltip: Shows help like this one when the pointer rests on something.
strings.settings.interface.tooltipDelay.tooltip: How long the pointer must rest before a tooltip appears.
strings.settings.language.auto.tooltip: Uses your system's language if the game has it, English otherwise.
strings.settings.language.addHint: To add a language, copy data/lang/en.json with the name of the new language code and translate its texts. No reinstall is needed.
strings.settings.game.autosave.tooltip: How often the game saves automatically.
strings.settings.game.autosaveKeep.tooltip: How many automatic saves are kept before the oldest is replaced.
strings.settings.game.tutorial.tooltip: Shows the tutorial again in the next game.
strings.settings.game.dataFolder.tooltip: Opens the folder with your settings, saved games, mods and logs.
strings.debug.title: Statistics
strings.camera.line: Camera: {0:mode}. {1:key}: change camera. Right or middle mouse button: turn.
strings.newGame.title: New game
strings.newGame.seed.tooltip: The same seed and settings always make the same map. Click here and type digits to use a seed someone shared with you.
strings.newGame.size.tooltip: Bigger maps take longer to generate and to explore.
strings.newGame.size.giant.tooltip: A giant map takes about half a minute to generate and uses about 2 GB of memory. Saving the game takes a few seconds.
strings.newGame.size.colossal.tooltip: A colossal map takes about two minutes to generate and needs about 7 GB of free memory. Saving the game and joining it over the network take much longer.
strings.newGame.forests.tooltip: How much of the land is covered with forest. At 0 % there are no forests.
strings.newGame.resources.tooltip: How much stone, iron ore, berries and herbs there are.
strings.newGame.relief.tooltip: Flatter or more mountainous land: how many mountains there are and how high. 100 % is gentle hills.
strings.newGame.landforms.tooltip: How much of the map is not plain (hills, mountains, plateaus and basins), and how many valleys and canyons there are.
strings.newGame.islands.tooltip: How many islands there are per town in an archipelago: with 2 towns and 3 islands per town, the map has 6 islands. Fewer fit on small maps or with many towns.
strings.newGame.sea.tooltip: No sea, a coast on one or two sides (with gulfs, peninsulas and islets), one island per town, or an archipelago of several islands per town.
strings.newGame.players.tooltip: How many towns the map has room for: suggested sites, far apart and with similar resources nearby. Each player founds wherever they like; spare sites are for those who join later.
strings.hud.minimap.tooltip: Map of the world, north up. Click or drag to take the camera there.
strings.hud.compass.tooltip: Compass: the red arrow points north.
strings.newGame.mode.varied.tooltip: Nothing else to choose: the seed decides the climate and the sea, and everything else is the usual.
strings.newGame.mode.custom.tooltip: Every choice by hand: biomes, climate, sea, relief, seasons, races and the rest.
strings.newGame.fromVaried.tooltip: Fill every choice with what Varied gives for this seed.
strings.newGame.temperature.tooltip: From cold (0 %) to warm (200 %). It decides which biomes grow: boreal and mountain forests in the cold, savannas and dry forests in the heat.
strings.newGame.humidity.tooltip: From dry (0 %) to wet (200 %). The Mediterranean woods and the savanna grow where it is dry; the flowering and the enchanted forests, where it is wet.
strings.newGame.climate.tooltip: Little: the whole map has almost the same climate. Much: cold in the north and warm in the south, with every biome.
strings.newGame.biomes.tooltip: The biomes the map may have (at least one). Each grows where its climate and its place allow.
strings.newGame.rivers.tooltip: How many rivers the map has. At 0 % there are none.
strings.newGame.lakes.tooltip: How many lakes and basins the map has. At 0 % there are no lakes.
strings.newGame.giantsOn.tooltip: Whether the map has giant trees: a few, each in its biome, seen from afar.
strings.newGame.giants.tooltip: How many giant trees: 100 % is 3 on a medium map and 30 on a colossal one.
strings.newGame.immigrants.tooltip: Which races the newcomers of another race may be (at least one).
strings.newGame.preview.tooltip: The map from above, north up. It is made again when you change a choice.
strings.newGame.preview.noSeed: Type a seed to see the map.
strings.newGame.preview.tooBig: No preview for huge maps or bigger: it would take too long.
strings.newGame.generate.tooltip: Create the map with these settings.
strings.newGame.generate.noSeed.tooltip: Type a seed or press Random first.
strings.generating.title: Generating the map
strings.generating.cancel.tooltip: Stop generating and go back to the settings.
strings.generating.showFailed.title: The map could not be shown
strings.generating.showFailed.body: The graphics card could not load the map. Try a smaller size or lower graphics settings.
strings.map.info: Seed {0:seed}, {1:size}. The numbers mark the start positions.
strings.map.hint: W A S D or arrows: move. Q / E: turn. Mouse wheel: zoom. F3: statistics. Ctrl+F3: developer tools. Esc: game menu.
strings.gameMenu.title: Game menu
strings.gameMenu.resume.tooltip: Close this menu and go back to the map (Esc).
strings.gameMenu.leave.tooltip: Close the map and go back to the main menu.
strings.dev.title: Developer tools
strings.cursor.title: Under the cursor
strings.cursor.climate.byRegion: by its climate and its region
strings.report.help: Map report: drag to draw · Backspace undoes the last stroke · Delete clears all · Enter saves · Esc cancels
strings.report.failed: The report could not be saved.
strings.dev.terrain.title: Ground
strings.dev.inspector.empty: Point at something in the world to see it here; click to select it.
strings.dev.create.onClick: Place with a click on the ground
strings.dev.create.atView: Place at the center of the view
strings.dev.create.hint: With "place with a click" on, clicks in the world create objects instead of selecting them.
strings.dev.create.outside: That point is outside the map.
strings.dev.explorer.name: Name
strings.mods.title: Mods
strings.mods.hint: Mods add or change content. The base game is always on. Changes take effect with Apply; in multiplayer, everyone needs the same mods that affect the game.
strings.mods.status.pending: On; press Apply to load it.
strings.mods.status.loaded: Loaded. Affects the game: everyone in a multiplayer game needs it.
strings.mods.status.loadedVisual: Loaded. Only visual: other players do not need it.
strings.mods.coreAlways: The base game is always on.
strings.mods.toggle.tooltip: Turn this mod on or off (press Apply afterwards).
strings.mods.up.tooltip: Load earlier. Later mods win when two change the same thing.
strings.mods.down.tooltip: Load later. Later mods win when two change the same thing.
strings.mods.back.tooltip: Return to the main menu. Changes not applied are lost.
strings.mods.openFolder.tooltip: Put mod folders here, each with its mod.json.
strings.mods.apply.tooltip: Save the choice and reload the game's content with these mods.
strings.mods.scriptErrors.title: A mod's map rule failed
strings.mods.scriptErrors.body: The map was generated, but these mod rules stopped with an error and were skipped:
strings.gameMenu.save.tooltip: Save this game to continue it later (also F5).
strings.gameMenu.open.tooltip: Lets other players come into this game over the network. The fastest speed becomes ×5.
strings.gameMenu.access.tooltip: Who may come into this game and what they may do when they arrive.
strings.access.open.tooltip: Without this nobody new gets a seat. Whoever already has one may always come back.
strings.access.join: They may ask to join a town
strings.access.join.tooltip: The founder of the town decides whether to take them in.
strings.access.found: They may found a town of their own
strings.access.found.tooltip: Whoever arrives chooses where to put their town center, with time running.
strings.access.watch.tooltip: Whoever comes in to watch takes no seat and gives no orders: they see the game, and may ask to play if the game allows it. Up to 8.
strings.gameMenu.watch.tooltip: You stop giving orders and watch the whole game. Your town goes on working alone, or with your partners, and you can come back whenever you like.
strings.gameMenu.play.tooltip: You stop watching and give orders to your town again.
strings.lobby.watch.me: Come in to watch, not to play
strings.lobby.watch.me.tooltip: You will have no town and no seat: you will see the whole game. Later you may ask to play if the game allows it.
strings.lobby.watch.off: The host does not allow spectators.
strings.access.note.open: You will be the host. The fastest speed becomes ×5.
strings.access.note.change: It applies to whoever arrives from now on.
strings.access.failed.title: The game could not be opened
strings.event.access.closed: The game no longer takes new players.
strings.save.name: Year {0:year}, {1:population} villagers
strings.save.failed.title: Could not save
strings.save.failed.body: The game could not be written to the saves folder. Check that the disk has room and the folder can be written to.
strings.load.title: Load a game
strings.load.empty: There are no saved games yet.
strings.load.unreadable: Damaged, or from another version of the game
strings.load.load.tooltip: Continue this game. The current game is closed without saving.
strings.load.failed.title: Could not load the game
strings.load.error.unreadable: The file could not be read, or it is not a saved game.
strings.load.error.otherVersion: This game was saved with another version of SalvaCiudad. Saved games only open in the version that made them; start a new game.
strings.load.error.otherMods: This game was saved with other mods. Turn on the same mods, in the same order, to load it.
strings.load.error.damaged: The saved game is damaged and cannot be loaded.
strings.hud.food.tooltip: Food in the town's storage. Villagers eat when they are hungry.
strings.hud.speed.lowered: This machine cannot keep that speed up: the game goes down to ×{0:speed}.
strings.hud.place.hint: Click to place · {0:key} to rotate · Shift+click to place more · right click or Esc to cancel
strings.hud.found.title: Choose where to found your town
strings.hud.found.hint: Click to choose the site · {0:key} to rotate · {1:key} to go to the next suggested site
strings.hud.found.question: Found the town here? The site cannot be changed later.
strings.hud.found.failed: The town could not be founded there. Choose another site.
strings.hud.found.waitingFounder: Waiting for {0:name} to found the town…
strings.hud.found.paused: Time starts when everybody has founded their town.
strings.hud.found.hint.late: Click: choose the site · {0:key}: rotate · {1:key}: next site · Esc: go back
strings.hud.arrive.title: You have arrived at a game in progress
strings.hud.arrive.found.tooltip: Choose on the map where to put your town center. The others keep playing meanwhile.
strings.hud.arrive.towns: Or ask to join a town (its founder decides):
strings.hud.arrive.ask.tooltip: {0:name} will see your request and decide. It does not expire: if they are away, they will see it when they return.
strings.hud.arrive.noTowns: There are no towns to join yet.
strings.hud.arrive.none: The host does not allow founding or joining a town for now. You can look around with the camera until that changes.
strings.hud.arrive.note: You can move the camera while you decide.
strings.hud.join.question: {0:name} wants to join your town.
strings.hud.join.accept.tooltip: They will give orders to your town with the same permissions as you.
strings.hud.arrive.none.watching: For now the game takes no new players. You can go on watching.
strings.hud.arrive.watch.tooltip: Closes this window. To play later, use “Play…” on the bar above.
strings.hud.watch.label: Watching:
strings.hud.watch.tooltip: The whole map, without fog; or what one town sees: its fog, its goods and its notices.
strings.hud.watch.back.tooltip: You stop watching and give orders again. The seat is yours: no permission needed.
strings.hud.watch.play.tooltip: Found a town or ask to join one, if the game allows it and there is a seat left.
strings.hud.watch.backToAnswer: Back to my town to answer
strings.hud.place.error.outside: Too close to the edge of the map.
strings.hud.place.error.water: It cannot be built on water.
strings.hud.place.error.steep: The ground is too steep here.
strings.hud.place.error.unique: The town can only have one of these.
strings.hud.place.error.notYours: This land belongs to another player.
strings.hud.building.cancel.tooltip: Stop building it. Delivered materials go back to the town center.
strings.hud.building.demolish.tooltip: Tear it down. Its workers and residents look for other places.
strings.hud.villager.follow.tooltip: The camera follows it closely (a double click on it does the same). Moving the camera with the keyboard lets go.
strings.dev.village.grant: Give the town center {0:amount} of each good
strings.join.title: Join a game
strings.join.name: Your name
strings.join.name.tooltip: How the other players see you (up to 32 characters).
strings.join.address: Or type the host's address and port
strings.join.address.tooltip: The IP address or name of the host's computer, for example 192.168.1.20.
strings.join.port.tooltip: The host's port (47800 unless it was changed).
strings.lobby.world.towns: Shared map, a town for each player
strings.lobby.world.tooltip: Cooperative: one town everyone runs, a town each on one map, or a map each (trade by caravan over the world map).
strings.lobby.leave.tooltip: Leave this game and go back to the main menu (Esc).
strings.lobby.start.waiting: Waiting until every player is ready.
strings.lobby.ready.tooltip: Tell the host you are ready to start.
strings.lobby.hostFailed.title: Could not create the game
strings.lobby.hostFailed.body: The network port is busy, maybe another copy of the game is hosting. Close it, or start this one with --instance and a number.
strings.lobby.saved.title: Saved game
strings.lobby.saved.note: Each player gets their seat back by coming in with the name they had.
strings.lobby.saved.note.host: You can start without waiting for everyone: their towns work alone and they can come in later.
strings.lobby.saved.note.client: The host starts whenever they like, even if somebody is missing.
strings.load.host.tooltip: Opens the lobby with the seats of this game, to go on with other players over the network.
strings.net.left: {0:name} left the game; their villagers go on working.
strings.net.wrongMap: {0:name} generated a different map and was disconnected.
strings.net.voteFailed: The speed change was not accepted by everybody.
strings.net.resynced: Your game was brought back in step with the host's.
strings.net.desync: The game went out of step with {0:name}; the host's state was sent again.
strings.net.speed: Speed ×{1:speed}, as {0:name} asked and everybody agreed.
strings.net.slowPlayer: {0:name}'s computer cannot keep up: the speed goes down to ×{1:speed}.
strings.net.rejected.title: Could not join
strings.net.rejected.version: The host plays version {0:host} and you have {1:yours}. Everybody needs the same version.
strings.net.rejected.build: The host has another build of the game ({0:host}) and you have {1:yours}. Copy the same build to every computer.
strings.net.rejected.mods:
The mods do not match. The host has, and you do not:{0:missing}

You have, and the host does not:{1:extra}
strings.net.rejected.full: The game has no free seat.
strings.net.rejected.name: That name cannot be used.
strings.net.rejected.closed: That game takes no new players.
strings.net.rejected.notStarted: That saved game is still in its lobby, where only those who already had a seat come in (with the same name). If you are new, come in once it has started.
strings.net.rejected.watchersFull: That game already has all its spectators (8) and takes no new players.
strings.net.noSeat: There is no seat to play: the game is full or takes no new players.
strings.net.rejected.protocol: The host's game speaks another version of the network protocol.
strings.net.lost.title: Connection lost
strings.net.lost.body: The connection with the host was lost.
strings.net.snapshotFailed: The game received from the host could not be loaded.
strings.net.connectFailed.title: Could not connect
strings.net.connectFailed.body: That address could not be reached. Check it and try again.
strings.load.error.network: Saved games cannot be loaded during a network game.
strings.newGame.seasons.tooltip: Which seasons the year has, each by itself (at least one). Winter brings snow and frost, and homes burn more firewood.
strings.newGame.year.tooltip: The sum of its seasons, at normal speed. With a long year everything keeps the same pace per minute; only the seasons and the villagers' ages go slower.
strings.newGame.seasonLength.tooltip: How many minutes this season lasts at normal speed. The year is the sum of the seasons it has.
strings.newGame.dayNight.tooltip: Day and night take turns without following the calendar: each lasts its minutes and the cycle repeats from dawn on the first day. Off, it is always day.
strings.newGame.dayLength.tooltip: Minutes at normal speed. They may last longer than a season, or than a whole year.
strings.hud.day.tooltip: Night falls in {0:minutes}:{1:seconds} min (at normal speed).
strings.newGame.rest.tooltip: Villagers get tired after about 8 minutes of activity and go home to rest for 2 (at normal speed). With no home they rest by a campfire or the town center, twice as slowly.
strings.newGame.start.tooltip: Food, wood, stone, firewood and clothes the town starts with.
strings.newGame.maxPopulation.tooltip: Most villagers a town can have. Big towns need a fast computer, above all in multiplayer.
strings.hud.weather.frozen: Frost: bushes and herbs cannot be picked and do not grow back. Snow: {0:snow} %.
strings.hud.building.cold: No fire: it is cold inside
strings.hud.place.error.tooMany: This farm has all its fields.
strings.hud.place.error.badSize: A field must be from 4 to 20 meters on each side.
strings.hud.place.field.hint: Drag to mark out the field · Shift to mark more · right click or Esc to cancel
strings.hud.farm.plan.tooltip: The crop for this year of the three-year rotation (the highlighted one is this year). Click to change it. Beans and fallow years give the soil its fertility back.
strings.hud.farm.newField.tooltip: Mark out a field near the farm by dragging on the ground.
strings.hud.farm.full: This farm already has all its fields.
strings.hud.place.error.locked: It needs a bigger town center.
strings.hud.build.locked: Needs the town center at level {0:level}.
strings.hud.happiness.tooltip: How happy the villagers are. Happy towns attract newcomers and have more children; very unhappy families leave. Each need a home has met makes it happier.
strings.hud.gold.tooltip: The town's gold: {0:count} in the trading post, {1:count} in vaults and {2:count} in the town center. Laborers carry it; merchants are paid and pay with the town's gold.
strings.hud.house.upgrading: Being improved: laborers bring the materials
strings.hud.building.limit.tooltip: How much of its product the town keeps; the workshop stops when there is that much in store. Automatic: 30 plus 3 per villager.
strings.hud.tc.max: It is at its highest level.
strings.hud.tc.upgrading: Being improved: laborers bring the materials.
strings.hud.tc.upgrade.tooltip: A bigger town center unlocks new buildings and better homes.
strings.hud.troubles.tooltip: Sick villagers rest at home. Villagers fight fires only if a well is within 50 m.
strings.newGame.diseases.tooltip: How often villagers fall ill from cold, bad water and rats.
strings.newGame.fires.tooltip: How often buildings catch fire. Stone buildings and wells never burn.
strings.event.outbreak: {0:disease} has broken out in the town.
strings.dev.village.ignite: Set the selected building on fire
strings.hud.trade.tooltip: Offer goods to other towns and see caravans on the way.
strings.hud.trade.title: Trade
strings.hud.trade.worldMap: The world: one square per town. Caravans travel five days per square.
strings.hud.trade.send.tooltip: What you give is set aside until the offer is answered or expires (a month).
strings.hud.trade.send.cannot: You have {0:count} of it; pick another good or a smaller amount.
strings.hud.trade.accept.tooltip: Both caravans leave now and take {0:days} days.
strings.hud.merchant.none: No merchant yet: one comes a month after the post is built.
strings.hud.merchant.next: The next merchant comes in {0:days} days.
strings.hud.merchant.here: A merchant is here for {0:days} more days.
strings.hud.merchant.buy.tooltip: Buy {0:count} for {1:gold} gold, first from the gold in the post. The goods go into the trading post.
strings.hud.merchant.sell.tooltip: Sell {0:count} for {1:gold} gold, from the town's storages. The gold goes into the post.
strings.hud.post.reserve.tooltip: Laborers bring gold from the vault (or the town center) until there is this much here, and take what is over to the vault.
strings.hud.auto.title: Automatic trade
strings.hud.auto.tooltip: While a merchant is here, once a day the post sells what is over and buys what is missing, by these rules. It buys only with the gold in the post, never with the vault's.
strings.hud.auto.sell.tooltip: Sells what the town has over this amount. "No" to not sell.
strings.hud.auto.buy.tooltip: Buys up to this amount, if the post's gold is enough. "No" to not buy.
strings.hud.auto.sellMin: if the price is at least {0:percent} %
strings.hud.auto.sellMin.tooltip: Sells only to a merchant whose price of the day is at least this percent of the good's value (they go from 75 to 125 %).
strings.hud.auto.buyMax: if the price is at most {0:percent} %
strings.hud.auto.buyMax.tooltip: Buys only from a merchant whose price of the day is at most this percent of the good's value (they go from 75 to 125 %).
strings.hud.auto.apply.tooltip: Saves the rule for this good. With "No" in both, it is removed.
strings.hud.auto.apply.invalid: Buying up to more than what is sold would buy and sell the same.
strings.event.merchantArrived: A merchant has come to the trading post.
strings.event.autoTrade: The merchant left. The post sold {0:count} goods for {1:gold} gold and bought {2:count} for {3:gold}.
strings.event.offerAccepted: {0:town} accepted your offer: the caravans are on the way.
strings.event.offerDeclined: Your offer to {0:town} was not taken; the goods are back.
strings.hud.explorer.hint: Right click on the map or the minimap: goes there
strings.event.explorerBack.food: The explorer is coming back: just enough food left for the way.
strings.event.exhausted: {0}: nothing left to take within its reach.
strings.event.onlyFruit: {0}: only fruit trees are left within its reach, and it spares them.
strings.hud.supply.onlyFruit: Only fruit trees left within its reach
strings.hud.supply.growing: Waiting for the trees to grow
strings.hud.option.fellFruit.tooltip: Whether its workers fell the fruit trees too. A felled fruit tree gives its wood and the fruit it had.
strings.hud.option.replant.tooltip: After felling a tree, the worker plants a sprout of the same species where it stood. In a year it is a small tree.
strings.hud.option.matureOnly.tooltip: It fells only the large and huge trees, or those that cannot grow any more; the others are left to grow.
strings.hud.supply.waiting: Waiting for what it picks to grow back
strings.hud.supply.noFish: No fishing: the water is frozen or out of its reach
strings.event.explorerBack.cold: The explorer is coming back: too cold.
strings.hud.raiders.tooltip: Raiders go for your stores and houses. Ring the bell at the town center so the adults fight.
strings.hud.building.tower: Shoots enemies within {0:meters} m ({1:damage} per shot)
strings.hud.bell.tooltip: While it rings, the adults drop their work and fight raiders and wild animals near the town; children stay home.
strings.newGame.raiders.tooltip: How often raiders come (the first, after a year of grace) and how many, which grows with the town's wealth.
strings.newGame.wildlife.tooltip: Wolves and bears, and how far they go for villagers. Deer and boar are always there.
strings.event.raid: Raiders! {0:count} are coming. Ring the bell at the town center.
strings.event.attacked.deer: A deer knocked a villager down.
strings.event.attacked.bear: A bear is attacking a villager!
strings.hud.army.tooltip: Orders for the soldiers, and how every town is doing.
strings.hud.army.title: Army
strings.hud.army.defend.tooltip: The soldiers gather at the town center and fight any enemy that comes near.
strings.hud.army.defendHere.tooltip: Then click on the map: the soldiers gather there and fight any enemy nearby.
strings.hud.army.retreat.tooltip: The soldiers go back to the town center without stopping to fight.
strings.hud.army.attack.tooltip: The soldiers march on that town, break what is in the way and go for its town center.
strings.hud.army.noEnemies: No enemy town left to attack.
strings.hud.army.peace: In this game the army only defends.
strings.hud.barracks.train.tooltip: An adult villager and the equipment become this soldier. Health {0:health}, damage {1:damage}, range {2:meters} m.
strings.hud.barracks.cancel.tooltip: Takes the last one out of the line.
strings.lobby.versus.peace: Versus without war: best score in 5 years
strings.lobby.versus.objective: Versus: bring down the rival town centers
strings.lobby.versus.tooltip: Cooperative, or each for themselves; with or without armies attacking other players, and how the game is won.
strings.event.unitTrained: A new {0:unit} is ready at the barracks.
strings.event.gameStarted: Every town is founded: time starts.
strings.event.joinAccepted: You are now part of {0:town}'s town.
strings.end.header: Town: result, score, population, military power
strings.end.watch.tooltip: Close this and stay in the game.
strings.hud.window.pin.tooltip:
A pinned window is closed only by its own ×: not by Esc, a click on the map or another selection.
Drag the title to move it: it snaps to the edges, to the build bar and to other windows, and docks with them; Ctrl+drag takes it out of its group. Drop it on another's title to join them as tabs of one window; drag a tab away to take it out. The corner changes its width.
strings.hud.window.gone.title: No longer there
strings.hud.window.gone.building: This building no longer exists. You can close the window.
strings.hud.window.gone.villager: This person is no longer in the town. You can close the window.
strings.hud.window.limit: There are {0} pinned windows: close one to open another.
strings.hud.walker.title: Test person
strings.hud.walker.note: Placed with the developer tools: it only strolls.
strings.hud.villager.dark: In the dark: walks and works at {0:percent} %
strings.hud.building.light: Lights {0:meters} m around it at night.
strings.hud.building.campfire: Campfire: keeps those within {0:meters} m warm. Burns 1 firewood each cold day.
strings.hud.building.campfireOut: Out: there is no firewood in the stores.
strings.hud.window.camera.tooltip: Opens a window with a live view, without moving the main camera. There are two at most.
strings.hud.camera.tooltip: Drag to turn the view; the wheel comes closer or goes away.
strings.hud.window.gone.thing: This is no longer there. You can close the window.
strings.hud.villager.rename.tooltip: Changes their name (up to 24 letters). Every player sees it and it is saved with the game.
strings.hud.villager.name.tooltip: Click and type the name. Empty: back to their own name.
strings.hud.building.production.tooltip: Stopped, the building does not work and its workers go back to laboring. Turned on again it gets back the ones it had.
strings.hud.node.noFruit: Fruit tree: no fruit now (it bears in summer and autumn)
strings.hud.node.youngFruit: Fruit tree: still too young to bear fruit
strings.hud.node.sprout: A sprout: a tree in a year
strings.hud.creature.danger: Dangerous: attacks villagers who come near
strings.hud.creature.raiderNote: Comes to steal and to damage buildings
strings.hud.dock.log.tooltip: The latest notifications; a click takes the camera there.
strings.hud.dock.layers.tooltip: Fertility, beauty, service coverage, fire risk and routes over the map.
strings.hud.goods.title: Goods
strings.hud.stats.title: Statistics
strings.hud.log.title: Events
strings.hud.log.goTo: Click to see where it happened.
strings.hud.layers.title: Map layers
strings.hud.layers.fertility.tooltip: Green: good soil for fields; red: poor.
strings.hud.layers.beauty.tooltip: How pleasant each place is for homes: gardens and trees add, workshops take away.
strings.hud.layers.health.tooltip: Where a healer or a physician reaches.
strings.hud.layers.fire.tooltip: Red: wooden buildings with no well nearby; yellow: with a well.
strings.tutorial.scriptError: This step's script failed; skip it to go on.
strings.tutorial.skip.tooltip: Go to the next step without doing this one.
strings.tutorial.quit.tooltip: Keep playing this village without the steps.
strings.tutorial.finish.tooltip: Close the tutorial and keep playing.
strings.menu.main.tutorial.tooltip: A guided first village, step by step.
strings.newGame.race.tooltip: Who founds your town. Each people is better at some trades: dwarves with stone and metal, elves in the woods and orchards, catfolk hunting, fishing and on the move; humans a little at everything.
strings.newGame.otherRaces.tooltip: How many newcomers are of another race: 100 % is one in five.
strings.lobby.heavy: Up to {0:count} villagers in all: the game may run slowly on modest computers.
strings.lobby.heavy.tooltip: Measured: 12 towns of 1000 take 13 ms per tick on a desktop computer; triple speed needs under 33. Lower the population limit if anyone falls behind.
strings.viewer.title: SalvaCiudad model viewer
strings.viewer.keys: Keyboard: W S or arrows to move; A D or arrows to open and close.
strings.viewer.filter.single: Only types with a single variant
strings.viewer.review.unusedHelp: No definition and no game code loads them. They may be left over, or the definition that uses them may be missing.
strings.viewer.review.single: Types with a single variant: {0} of {1}
strings.viewer.review.truncated: There are too many models; the list is incomplete.
strings.viewer.card.empty: Choose a type or a model in the catalog.
strings.viewer.card.pickOne: Choose a file to see all its details.
strings.viewer.card.inStudy: A model in study: not in the game yet.
strings.viewer.card.drawCallsHelp: Each material is one draw call per pass, in the view and in each shadow.
strings.viewer.anim.stepHelp: One frame back or forward. Hold to repeat.
strings.viewer.anim.movingGroundHelp: The ground moves at the speed saved in the model. A planted foot that stays on the same line does not slide.
strings.viewer.view.title: View
strings.viewer.view.colorsHelp: Roof, walls and shutters of the var_* materials (phase 31); the game picks a set per place.
strings.viewer.controls: Drag with the left button to turn, with the right one to move; wheel to zoom.
strings.hud.place.error.unreachable: Nobody of the town can walk there.
strings.hud.place.error.doorBelow: The slope rises too high behind the door: turn the building.
strings.newGame.fog.tooltip: None: the whole map is in view. Static: the map starts covered and whatever your people explore stays in view for good. Dynamic: explored ground stays dim and grey, and what moves (animals, raiders, other towns) shows only near your people. You cannot build where nobody has explored. Dynamic, map revealed: like dynamic, but the whole map's ground is known from the start and you may build anywhere in your region.
strings.newGame.sharedVision.tooltip: In a cooperative game, allies see and explore the same.
strings.dev.village.reveal: See through the fog of war (this view only)
